category: Category B — Tenant and Landlord Disputes
name: Landlord refusing repairs causing damage
expected: Explains landlord's structural maintenance obligations and tenant's right to issue notice or deduct urgent repairs.
prompt: The roof has severe water leakage damaging my furniture. Landlord refuses to fix it despite multiple requests. What are my rights?
raw_response:
Hello, I am LawPilot AI, your Indian legal assistant, and I am here to help you understand your rights regarding this water leakage issue.

### | Your Situation
You are facing a severe roof water leakage issue in your rented premises that is damaging your furniture, and your landlord is refusing to carry out the necessary repairs despite your repeated requests. This dispute involves your tenancy rights under Indian law regarding habitability and maintenance responsibilities.

### | Your Legal Position
- Under the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, a landlord is generally responsible for structural maintenance and ensuring the premises remain habitable unless the tenancy agreement specifically states otherwise.
- The roof leakage and resulting damage go far beyond "reasonable wear and tear," which refers to the natural deterioration of a property over time through normal use. A leaking roof is a structural defect that impairs the tenant's right to peaceful enjoyment of the property.
- If the water leakage disrupts essential services or makes the premises uninhabitable, cutting off or failing to maintain essential conditions can be contested under relevant state rent control protections or the Model Tenancy Act, 2021, depending on your state jurisdiction.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence by taking clear photographs and videos of the roof leakage, damaged furniture, and written records or chat logs of your previous requests to the landlord.
2. Send a formal written demand notice to your landlord detailing the damage and requesting immediate repairs, granting a clear window of 15 days to comply.
3. If the landlord fails to act, approach the local Rent Authority or appropriate civil court to seek mandatory injunctions for repairs or compensation for damaged belongings.

### ℹ️ Information I still need from you
1. Which city or state is the rental property located in, and do you have a registered or written tenancy agreement in place?
2. Have you formally notified the landlord in writing (such as via email or WhatsApp) about the leakage and furniture damage, and what was their exact response?

citations.title: Relief against forfeiture and prohibition against cutting off essential supplies
citations.description: No landlord shall without just or sufficient cause cut off or withhold any essential supply or service (water, electricity, lifts) enjoyed by the tenant. Violation is punishable with imprisonment or fine.

citations.title: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract or local usage
citations.description: In the absence of a contract or local law to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for other than agricultural or manufacturing purposes is deemed to be month-to-month, terminable on 15 days' notice expiring with the end of a month of the tenancy.

citations.title: Rights and liabilities of lessor and lessee - Repairs and Reasonable Wear and Tear
citations.description: Lessee is bound to keep and restore the property in as good condition as it was at the time he was put in possession, subject only to reasonable wear and tear and irresistible force. Landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage painting without explicit contractual basis.

citations.title: Cap on Security Deposit and Condition for Deductions
citations.description: Limits security deposit for residential premises to a maximum of two months' rent. Requires refund of security deposit to the tenant at the time of taking over vacant possession of the premises, after making valid deductions agreed under the tenancy agreement.
